title: Reconcile intermittent tenant fanout after service-account delegation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Intermittent multi-tenant attribution fanout observed when requests are made using delegated service account tokens. Symptoms: single API request appears as usage against multiple projects/orgs (duplicate token fanout), inflating billed tokens and tripping quota guards. Root cause hypothesis: token binding lookup occasionally returns a stale multi-tenant mapping when delegation tokens are accepted through our public gateway during a brief race against the tenant-binding cache refresh. This ticket scopes the investigation, reproducible test harness, fix, and rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create org A and project A1 and org B with project B1. 2) Create a delegated service account token for A that is also usable by an automation runner (service-account delegation). 3) Rapidly rotate delegation tokens and replay a burst of identical requests through the edge gateway while toggling project attachments in the admin panel (simulates background binding refresh). 4) Observe /metrics and billing attribution table: some requests are recorded against B1 as well as A1. Reproducible locally with the attached harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/qa-tools/tree/tenant-fanout-repro
impact: medium-to-high: Increases customer bills unexpectedly and may cause quota enforcement to hit wrong projects. Affects hosted customers using delegated automations and internal infra runs. Incidents in Feb 2026 resulted in two customers reporting strange overage alerts and a support ticket spike (~12 customers potentially impacted).
proposed_solution: 1) Harden token->tenant canonicalization at ingress: require authoritative claim resolution from tenant service before emitting attribution events. 2) Make tenant-binding cache writes atomic and use a short in-memory grace TTL during rotation windows. 3) Add strong dedup keys for per-request attribution events (including token id, request-id, and authoritative tenant-id) so downstream metering deduplicates transient fanout. 4) Add a regression test in billing-service that simulates token rotation races.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproducer shows 0 cross-project attributions for 100k-request bursts under rotation scenarios.
- New unit/integration tests passing in CI.
- No increase in end-to-end latency >5ms at gateway median for delegated token path.
- Observability: alert fires if cross-project attribution rate >0.1% in prod after rollout.
- Change signed off by Billing PM and Security.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy soft guards behind feature-flag in canary region (us-west-2) for 24 hours, collect metrics. Phase 2: Toggle authoritative tenant lookup by default and keep dedupe logic enabled for 48 hours. Phase 3: Full rollout globally with automatic rollback if cross-project attribution regresses beyond baseline. Plan PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287
tests:
- Unit tests for cache atomicity and dedupe key generation.
- Integration test that uses the qa-tools harness to run token-rotation bursts (runs nightly).
- Load test under gateway to assert latency and p95 remains within SLA.
- Synthetic checks: continuously run reproducer in staging to compare attribution histogram.
monitoring: Dashboards updated: Billing Attribution (new panels for token-id collision rates, per-token-project count histogram). Alerts: billing.attribution.cross_project_rate > 0.1% for 30m. Links: https://grafana.redwood-inference/internal/d/attribution/billing-attribution
